desc:
For every non-empty contiguous subarray of nums, compute the bitwise XOR of its elements. Return the sum of all these XOR values, modulo 1,000,000,007.

nums = [1, 2, 3]
subarray XORs: 1, 2, 3, 1^2 = 3, 2^3 = 1, 1^2^3 = 0
sum = 10
result = 10
hints: There are n(n+1)/2 subarrays, so listing them is too slow for the largest inputs. Write each subarray XOR with prefix XORs.
The XOR of the block between prefix positions i < j is P[i] ^ P[j], so you need the sum of P[i] ^ P[j] over all pairs of the n + 1 prefix values.
XOR works bit by bit. For each bit position, if c of the prefix values have that bit set, exactly c * (n + 1 - c) pairs differ in that bit, contributing 2bit each.
editorial: Let P[0] = 0 and P[i] the XOR of the first i elements. The XOR of the subarray occupying positions i..j-1 is P[i] ^ P[j], so the requested sum equals the sum of P[i] ^ P[j] over all unordered pairs of the n + 1 prefix values.

The XOR of two numbers has bit b set iff exactly one of them has it. If c prefix values have bit b set and n + 1 - c do not, then c * (n + 1 - c) pairs contribute 2b. Summing over the 30 relevant bits (values up to 109 fit in 30 bits) gives the answer modulo 109 + 7. This is O(30 n) time and O(n) space, compared with O(n2) for pairwise XORs.
